source_text: De eo quod scriptum est: Moyses famulus meus defunctus est. Et Moysi obitum oportet nos enarrare; nisi intellexerimus quomodo moritur Moyses, non poterimus advertere quomodo regnat Iesus. Si consideres Hierusalem subversam, altare destitutum, nusquam sacrificia nec hostias nec libamina, nusquam sacerdotes nec Levitas: cum haec vides cessare, dicito: Moyses famulus Dei defunctus est. Cum vero videris introire gentes ad fidem, ecclesias exstrui, altaria pretioso Christi sanguine consecrari, sacerdotes verbum Dei ministrantes — tunc dicito quia Iesus post Moysen suscepit principatum, non Iesus filius Nave sed Iesus filius Dei. Cum videris pascha nostrum immolatum Christum et azyma sinceritatis, fructus tricesimos sexagesimos centesimos, viduas virgines martyres, semen Israel ex Deo natum, sabbatizare populum ab operatione peccati — dicito: Moyses defunctus est et Iesus filius Dei obtinet principatum. In libello non canonico duo Moyses: unus vivus in spiritu, alius mortuus in corpore — littera legis inanis est Moyses mortuus; lex spiritalis est Moyses vivens.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning that which written-is: Moses servant my dead-is. And of-Moses death it-behooves us to-narrate; unless we-shall-have-understood how dies Moses, not we-shall-be-able to-perceive how reigns Jesus. If you-consider Jerusalem overthrown, altar abandoned, nowhere sacrifices nor victims nor libations, nowhere priests nor Levites: when these you-see to-cease, say: Moses servant of-God dead-is. When however you-shall-have-seen to-enter nations unto faith, churches to-be-built, altars with-precious of-Christ blood consecrated, priests word of-God ministering — then say that Jesus after Moses took principate, not Jesus son of-Nun but Jesus son of-God. When you-shall-have-seen passover our sacrificed Christ and unleavened-things of-sincerity, fruits thirties sixties hundreds, widows virgins martyrs, seed Israel out-of God born, to-sabbath-keep people from working of-sin — say: Moses dead-is and Jesus son of-God obtains principate. In booklet not canonical two Moses: one living in spirit, other dead in body — letter of-law empty-is Moses dead; law spiritual-is Moses living.
pass_b_english: On what is written: [[Moses my servant is dead >> Bible:Joshua 1:2]]. We must recount Moses’ death; unless we understand how Moses dies, we cannot see how Jesus reigns. If you look on Jerusalem overthrown, the altar abandoned, nowhere sacrifices or offerings or drink-offerings, nowhere priests or Levites — when you see all this cease, say: [[Moses the servant of God is dead >> Bible:Joshua 1:2]]. But when you see the nations enter faith, churches raised, altars consecrated by [[Christ’s precious blood >> Bible:1 Peter 1:19]], priests ministering the word of God by the Spirit’s grace — then say that Jesus has taken the principate after Moses: not Jesus son of Nun, but Jesus the Son of God. When you see that [[our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed >> Bible:1 Corinthians 5:7]] and we eat [[unleavened bread of sincerity and truth >> Bible:1 Corinthians 5:8]]; when you see the church’s fruits [[thirtyfold, sixtyfold, a hundredfold >> Bible:Matthew 13:23]] — widows, virgins, martyrs; when you see Israel’s seed multiplied from those [[born not of blood nor of the will of flesh, but of God >> Bible:John 1:13]]; when you see God’s people keeping a sabbath rest not by idle withdrawal from common life but by rest from the work of sin — then say: Moses is dead, and Jesus the Son of God holds the principate. In a certain booklet outside the canon the figure is drawn of two Moseses — one alive in spirit, one dead in body. The empty letter of the law is Moses dead in the body; if you can [[remove the veil >> Bible:2 Corinthians 3:16]] and understand that [[the law is spiritual >> Bible:Romans 7:14]], that is Moses alive in the spirit.
